question: When is the next protocol upgrade, how do validators vote it in, and what SDK-upgrade deadlines must developers meet?

golden.answer:
As of 2026-11-10, Bell (Protocol 30) is live on Testnet after the November 3 upgrade. The next announced Mainnet vote is November 23, 2026 at 17:00 UTC, and Mainnet still runs Protocol 29. Validators coordinate the proposed version and time, then agree on the upgrade through network consensus. A software release or an announced vote alone does not activate the protocol.

The Bell guide calls for compatible SDKs before November 3 for Testnet integrations and before November 23 for Mainnet integrations. CAP-0088 adds new StellarValue variants carrying millisecond close time inside the ledger header’s scpValue. Older SDKs may fail to decode the new encoding.

The dated example is illustrative. A later answer should report the state supported at its observation time.
keyFacts: Reports the relevant network's next announced vote or its absence as of the source date.
Explains how validator agreement activates a network upgrade.
Reports the published SDK deadlines for the relevant networks.
Explains why a compatible SDK is required.
avoid: Do NOT claim a completed upgrade is the next scheduled vote.
Do NOT invent a later protocol vote date without a dated primary source.
Do NOT confuse protocol upgrade voting with SEP/CAP approval or a software release alone.
Do NOT present version-, provider-, interface-, or availability-sensitive observations as timeless; date the changeable part without weakening stable protocol or historical facts.
golden.notes: Check the latest official upgrade guide and operational status. Report the target network for each vote and SDK deadline. Bell’s Testnet deadline is historical as of 2026-11-10. Accept a later dated status or reschedule. CAP-0088 changes nested StellarValue encoding in scpValue while the direct LedgerHeader fields stay the same.
